speaker: Doctor
text: I am reviewing the newborn with a generalized rash. To begin my assessment, can you tell me when the rash first appeared and if the baby has any fever or seems irritable?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see the infant is 4 days old with a rash that started yesterday. Can you describe the appearance of the rash, such as whether it is blisters, pustules, or red spots, and check if there are any lesions on the palms or soles?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The rash description of pustules on an erythematous base sparing the palms and soles in a 4-day-old is highly suggestive of neonatal cephalic pustulosis or possibly early syphilis, though the sparing of palms/soles makes congenital syphilis less likely. To rule out serious infections like bacterial sepsis or viral etiologies, I need to check for systemic involvement.

REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential, Blood_Culture, Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal CBC and blood cultures are reassuring against bacterial sepsis. Given the mother's lack of prenatal care, I need to rule out congenital syphilis despite the rash sparing the palms and soles.

REQUEST TEST: VDRL, Rapid_Plasmin_Reagent_Test, Darkfield_Microscopy

speaker: Doctor
text:
The negative syphilis serology and darkfield microscopy effectively rule out congenital syphilis. Given the normal CBC and blood cultures, this clinical picture is classic for benign neonatal cephalic pustulosis (neonatal acne), which typically presents with erythematous pustules sparing the palms and soles in the first few weeks of life.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Cephalic Pustulosis
